we present a new deep neural network approach to anatomical brain segmentation that outperforms the state-of-the-art.

we propose a novel approach based on a deep neural network that automatically segment magnetic resonance images of the brain into anatomical structures without the need of a prior non-linear registration.
we have developed a novel deep learning approach to automatically segment MR images of the human whole brain into anatomical sub-regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of deep learning methods for the segmentation of anatomical brain regions from magnetic resonance images.
the development of novel methods for the automatic segmentation of the human brain using deep neural network architectures.
the development of a novel deep learning method for the automatic segmentation of anatomical brain regions from MR images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is the first one to tackle the anatomically segmentation of the whole human brain using deep learning.
the use of deep neural networks is a promising approach in medical image analysis, and that our method is a step in this direction.
our method outperforms the current state of the art in anatomical brain segmentation and that the results are competitive with multi-atlas based segmentation methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach is the first to use deep neural networks in a fully automatic manner to segment anatomical structures from MR images.
our technique is able to segment the brain in 3.5 seconds on average, while achieving competitive segmentation performance.

we present an automatic approach for the anatomical segmentation using a deep neural network that does not require any registration of the images and that is based on a novel combination of different scales and spatial information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of deep learning and large-scale datasets can yield state-of-the-art results in a fully automated fashion.
deep learning techniques are a powerful tool to automatically learn features that can be used to segment MR images of the human head into anatomical structures.
deep networks can be used for a wide range of tasks and not only for image classification, such as in the case of the popular AlexNet.
